issues.legal_issue: Continuous cohabitation as spouses supports a presumption of a marital relationship and the legitimacy of their children, and omissions in earlier documents or evidence that does not deny cohabitation do not rebut that presumption.
material_facts: The man and the woman lived together under the same roof and cohabited for many years.
Children, including the person through whom the claimant derived title, were born to them.
A will and a later compromise did not mention the woman or her children.
The witnesses relied on to challenge the relationship did not deny that the man and woman lived together.
The first appellate court accepted the presumption and decreed the title suit, but the High Court reversed that decision; the matter reached the Supreme Court in an appeal concerning the title suit.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances relied on to rebut the presumption were not relevant or sufficient to destroy it. The appeal was allowed, and the first appellate court’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Continuous cohabitation and living together as husband and wife give rise to a presumption of a marital relationship. The absence of references to the woman or her children in a will or compromise, and testimony that does not deny their cohabitation, do not rebut that presumption or undermine the legitimacy of the children. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: title_suit_appeal and prolonged_cohabitation and children_born_of_cohabitation and documents_omit_partner_and_children and witnesses_do_not_deny_cohabitation

predicates.title_suit_appeal: A civil appeal concerns a title suit in which a lower appellate court accepted a marital-relationship presumption and the High Court reversed that decision.
predicates.prolonged_cohabitation: A man and a woman lived together and cohabited for many years.
predicates.children_born_of_cohabitation: Children were born to the man and woman while they were living together.
predicates.documents_omit_partner_and_children: A will and a compromise document did not refer to the woman or her children.
predicates.witnesses_do_not_deny_cohabitation: The witnesses relied on to challenge the relationship did not deny that the man and woman lived together.

issues.definition: When a title-suit appeal involves prolonged cohabitation and children born of that cohabitation, omissions from documents and testimony that does not deny cohabitation leave the presumption of a marital relationship and the children’s legitimacy standing.
